newsitem.title: UK: IPE Brent crude closes at day's highs, wait API's.
newsitem.headline: IPE Brent crude closes at day's highs, wait API's.

text.p: IPE August Brent crude oil ended at the days highs following good volume shortcovering in the last few minutes trade. The bullish tone was U.S. led where expectations for overnight U.S. weekly statistics were supportive, brokers said.
The Aug Brent contract gained some 20 cents to close at $18.39 a barrel, above key trendline support at $18.31.
"This is technically a constructive close but we'll see what happens with the API's," one broker commented.

Dealers expectations for the weekly statistics from the American Petroleum Institute, due out after markets close on Tuesday, were bullish. They included a draw of one to two million barrels on gasoline stocks and a drop on crude stocks of two to three million barrels. Distillates (heating oil and diesel) are expected to build by one to 2.5 million barrels.
The data is for the week ended July 4.
"The Americans seem to believe the predictions. They gained good ground. We'll wait and see," another broker said.
News that talks between U.N. and Iraqi government officials are still continuing was slightly bullish.
"The market did not react much but it didn't go down," the broker added.
Iraq's ambassador to the United Nations, Nizar Hamdoon, said Tuesday that U.N./Iraqi talks were continuing, though he couldn't say whether agreement on the key aid distribution plan was near.
"They are working out issues, both logistical and on political points," said Hamdoon. "But I am not aware of the outcome of today's meetings."
Ambassador Hamdoon said he was unaware of any major snags in the talks. He said he could not say when the distribution plan will be delivered to the U.N. secretary-general for approval.

Approval of the plan is necessary to allow the second round of Iraqi oil exports under the so-called oil-for-food deal which allows Iraq to sell up to $2.14 billion of oil over 180 days to buy and distribute aid under strict U.N. supervision.
